name: Philadelphia and Lancaster Turnpike
note: Opened 1795. FHWA calls it the first important turnpike and the first long-distance broken-stone road built in America to formal plans. The line is a schematic through towns on that corridor, not a surveyed 1795 centerline.
source_label: FHWA, Carl Rakeman caption, 1795 Philadelphia and Lancaster Turnpike

name: National Road, first construction
note: Construction began at Cumberland, Maryland in 1811; the first contract covered about the first 10 miles. This segment is the start of that corridor toward Uniontown, drawn schematically.
source_label: FHWA National Road fact sheet

name: National Road to Wheeling
note: The Cumberland-to-Wheeling section was completed in 1818. Towns are the documented corridor; the line is schematic, not the historic centerline.
source_label: FHWA National Road fact sheet

name: Lincoln Highway
states: Florida, Idaho, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Wyoming, West Virginia, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Nebraska, New Jersey, Oregon
note: The Lincoln Highway Association dedicated the coast-to-coast auto trail on 31 Oct 1913. The line is the modern U.S. 30 centerline from Natural Earth, a corridor proxy, not the 1913 alignment mile for mile. Designation, not a paving date.
source_label: FHWA, From Names to Numbers; Lincoln Highway dedicated 1913
